summary: Closed the read-index thread and reselected onto participant eligibility. New investigation @removed_member_forward tests whether a node the configuration no longer contains can still have proposals accepted. Two source facts make it concrete: node.run() disables the proposal channel when the node learns it was removed but re-enables it on any observed leader change (with the in-tree comment conceding the logic is 'not very sound and likely has bugs'), and neither stepFollower's forward path nor stepLeader's MsgProp handler checks sender membership. A focused probe against the real FSM confirmed both halves: after applyConfChange removed node 3 from a leader's config (voters [1 2], Progress[3] deleted) a MsgProp with From=3 was accepted (err=nil, one entry appended), and a removed follower still forwarded a local MsgProp to its leader. Recorded as a behaviour fact plus an open necessary gap, with the interpretation deliberately left conditional/unresolved: the decisive question is whether the library owes sender eligibility or the application owns that authorization, so no defect is asserted and severity is not assessed. The retry-growth finding and its measurements are unchanged.
